answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded reputation: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before transacting, slashed if peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts on a lonely knoll of low trust, rate-limited and unable to attest others until it builds a record of verified honest work. Trust then grows like a trellis, each confirmed task adding a rung that raises its limits, while a meadow of cheap, unverified identities earns no weight. Faking thousands of agents means funding thousands of bonds and slowly earning trust for each, which costs far more than the attack can gain.
